target_moa.text: Omadacycline is a tetracycline-class (aminomethylcycline) antibacterial that binds the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, inhibiting binding of aminoacyl-tRNA and blocking bacterial protein synthesis; it retains activity in the presence of tetracycline efflux and ribosomal protection (Tet(O)) mechanisms

citations.quote: Omadacycline is a tetracycline antibacterial drug and exerts its effects by binding to the 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome and blocking protein synthesis.
As a class, tetracyclines bind to the bacterial ribosome 30S subunit and inhibit binding of aminoacyl-transfer ribonucleic acid, blocking bacterial protein synthesis.

Omadacycline was shown to inhibit protein synthesis in a cell-free system irrespective of the presence or absence of Tet(O), whereas tetracycline activity was significantly reduced in the presence of Tet(O)
Omadacycline is a novel semi-synthetic tetracycline antibacterial compound prepared by [REDACTED](b) (4).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) include nausea, vomiting, infusion site reactions, transaminase elevations, hypertension, headache, diarrhea, insomnia, and constipation. In the ABSSSI trials nausea occurred in 21.9% (vs 8.7% linezolid) and vomiting in 11.4% (vs 3.9%). The key serious safety concern was a mortality imbalance in the CABP trial (2% NUZYRA vs 1% moxifloxacin).

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥2%) are nausea, vomiting, infusion site reactions, alanine aminotransferase increased, aspartate aminotransferase increased, gamma-glutamyl transferase increased, hypertension, headache, diarrhea, insomnia, and constipation. (6.1)
